answer: A surety bond no operator can self-supply is one defence. Before a new seat attests, two sponsors from clusters with no shared operator must each lock a bond worth a month of expected yield, slashed if that seat proves duplicate. A farm mints ten thousand keys for pennies but cannot conjure ten thousand independent sponsors who risk capital, so a sybil cost moves from compute to borrowed trust. The ledger behaves like shale: copies crumble, one bonded layer holds. Each bond is a mirror, casting a sponsor record back at them, and crowded farms sink into a shallow lagoon of self-dealing.
